title: Machine-learning selection of a six-protein panel for atherosclerosis severity and patient stratification
summary: Five machine-learning classifiers integrated clinical and serum-proteomic data from carotid atherosclerotic stenosis (60 participants), dyslipidemia (55) and healthy controls (66). A consensus approach identified a six-protein panel (B2M, GPV, MMP9, PLF4, TSP1 and fibrinogen/FB isoforms) that distinguished the atherosclerosis group from the comparison groups, with reported ROC-AUC above 0.9 across the tested classifiers. Protein levels were evaluated by flow cytometry and ELISA in an independent external cohort that included patients with acute atherothrombotic stroke.
ai_technology: Five machine-learning classifiers: Naive Bayes, linear SVM, random forest, Extra Trees and AdaBoost
organization: Biomedical Research and Innovation Institute of Cadiz, University of Cadiz and collaborating clinical institutions

evidence.tested: A consensus approach identified a six-protein panel (B2M, GPV, MMP9, PLF4, TSP1 and fibrinogen/FB isoforms) that distinguished the atherosclerosis group from the comparison groups, with reported ROC-AUC above 0.9 across the tested classifiers.
evidence.unknown: The discovery cohorts were small (60 atherosclerosis, 55 dyslipidemia and 66 healthy controls); external validation supports the measured panel but does not establish population-wide performance, prospective clinical utility, or improved patient outcomes. The proteins have prior biological associations, so the finding is the specific integrated panel and cohort discrimination rather than discovery of six new proteins or a new mechanism.
evidence.ai_role: Five classifiers integrated clinical and serum-proteomic features and selected a consensus six-protein panel for patient-group discrimination. The authors then evaluated the selected proteins in an independent clinical cohort using flow cytometry and ELISA.
